newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent climbs over $19, little blockade impact.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent climbs over $19, little blockade impact.

text.p: IPE Brent futures climbed above $19 a barrel on Monday morning for the first time in nearly six weeks.
But dealers said underlying strength had pushed the market higher rather than the blockade of Sullom Voe oil terminal by local fishermen.
June Brent was up 20 cents a barrel at $19.13 at 0943 GMT having peaked a few minutes earlier at $19.17.
The blockade "might add a bit of fuel to the fire" but most of the gains were due to better fundamentals and technical strength, said a broker.
Physical Brent climbed sharply higher last week amid fears North Sea loadings programmes issued this week would reveal a shortfall of around 24 cargoes in June.
Physical Brent was being valued at just eight cents below forward prices compared to discounts of up to $1 a barrel around a month ago.
Technical strength was also helping Brent futures, after prices managed to clamber above the $18.75 last week. The next upside target was $19.45 to $19.50 a barrel, said dealers.

Launch of new wargames by Iran in the Gulf on Sunday was potentially supportive but not having any immediate impact, said brokers. A top U.S. military commander pledged to defend the strategic Straits of Mormuz against any Iranian threat.
Meanwhile, gas oil was up $1.75 a tonne on June at $169.25 at 0954 GMT with resistance seen at $171.
Dealers said Rotterdam barges were pegged at parity to the IPE May contract, which expires at noon on Monday and is some $2.50 a tonne over June.
